A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments with Pythia-6.9B and Mistral-7B-sft, including benchmark scores, training dynamics and generated examples in Section 5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G, and reports additional hyperparameter sensitivity results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The PRO objective, hyper-response construction and PRO-P/B/S implementations remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same practical approximation setting the hyper-response implicit reward to zero. The added analysis does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Anthropic-HH and UltraFeedback across pairwise, binary and scalar feedback, including extreme binary imbalance. Evaluation benchmarks in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged. The additional hyperparameter configurations reuse existing scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain SFT, DPO, KTO and NCA; scalar-feedback comparisons retain NCA, and the imbalance experiment retains KTO. Newly cited DPO variants are discussed but not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Beyond v1's existing sweeps, v2 Appendix E reports joint α–β configurations: (2.5, 0.003), (7.5, 0.001), (22.5, 0.0003) for pairwise feedback, and (17.5, 0.003), (52.5, 0.001), (157.5, 0.0003) for 1%-desired binary feedback. The retained experiments' training and evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix E extends v1 Appendix F's regularizer analysis with empirical checks of whether increasing α while decreasing β preserves performance. Existing imbalance tests, response-count comparisons, reward trajectories and qualitative cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests for the reported comparisons. The additional sensitivity results likewise provide point estimates without new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Appendix E adds pairwise win rates of 53.21%, 52.97% and 53.65% under its three α–β configurations. For 1%-desired feedback, it adds 56.51% and 56.33% alongside the previously reported 57.21%. These are configuration-specific results, not same-setting improvements; existing tables, plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 replaces Appendix B.1's derivation with a log-sigmoid-based proof, adds Corollary B.2 and its constructive general-feedback bound on α, and restores missing β factors in Appendix C's regularizer gradient, changing v1 Equation (30) to v2 Equation (31). These refine the theory while retaining the main theorem statements.

C1.justification: Section 6 locally narrows the description of PRO from being 'free from' underdetermination to 'mitigating' it, and emphasizes length-exploitation and performance-stability findings. The abstract and contribution list retain the central decomposition, unified-feedback and superiority claims, so this qualification is limited.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that sufficiently large α can trade off with β, simplifying tuning. Section 4.1 further positions the inability to distinguish unobserved responses as a limitation shared with existing methods. The earlier confidence-based interpretation of the empirical-to-population sampling ratio is removed; the KTO degradation explanation is retained after relocation.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds practical tuning guidance and explicit α–β configurations for the sensitivity results. Appendix D's implementation details and the shared training settings remain unchanged, and no new code-access or hardware information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references covering DPO variants and their unification through reference-model selection. Section 6 connects these works to possible future improvements of PRO. Existing references and Appendix A's principal research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Substantial prose rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, experimental narrative, discussion and proof appendix. The KTO explanation moves from v1 Appendix E into Section 5.1, subsequent appendices are relabeled, and explanations of regularizer completeness and hyperparameter tuning are expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1 illustrating aggregation into a hyper response. The five existing figures retain their plotted content and become Figures 2–6. Tables retain their structure and contents, with limited repositioning and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing paper through a constructive α bound, correction of the missing gradient factor, limited α–β sensitivity evidence and a helpful hyper-response schematic. These improve theoretical precision, explanation and tuning guidance. The central method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged, and the added sensitivity results lack uncertainty estimates, limiting the overall gain.
